subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which group of materials is magnetic (attracted to a magnet and can be magnetised)?
questions.explain: The common magnetic materials are iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.

questions.q: In what direction do magnetic field lines point outside a bar magnet?
options: From the north pole to the south pole
From the south pole to the north pole
In random directions around the magnet
questions.explain: By convention, magnetic field lines run from north to south outside the magnet.

questions.q: Which material is used as the core of an electromagnet?
questions.explain: Soft iron is used because it magnetises strongly and loses its magnetism when the current is switched off.

questions.q: Which equation gives the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
questions.explain: The force equals magnetic flux density × current × length of conductor in the field.

questions.q: What is Fleming's left-hand rule used to find?
options: The direction of the force (motion) on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field
The size of the induced voltage in a transformer
The number of turns on a solenoid
questions.explain: The left-hand rule relates the directions of field, current and the resulting force (motion).

questions.q: Which equation correctly links the voltages and turns of a transformer?
questions.explain: The primary and secondary voltages are in the same ratio as their numbers of turns.

questions.q: The magnetic field produced outside a current-carrying solenoid is most similar to the field of which object?
questions.explain: A solenoid produces a field like that of a bar magnet, with a north and south pole at its ends.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a permanent magnet and an induced magnet?
options: A permanent magnet keeps its magnetism, while an induced magnet is only magnetic while near a magnet
An induced magnet is always stronger than a permanent magnet
A permanent magnet only attracts, while an induced magnet only repels
An induced magnet has no poles
questions.explain: Induced magnetism is temporary and disappears when the magnetic material is removed from the field.

questions.q: Why is soft iron, rather than steel, used for the core of an electromagnet?
options: It loses its magnetism quickly when the current is switched off
It stays magnetised permanently after use
It carries the electric current instead of the coil
It stops the coil from getting hot
questions.explain: Soft iron is easily magnetised and demagnetised, so the electromagnet can be switched on and off.

questions.q: What shape is the magnetic field pattern around a long straight current-carrying wire?
options: Straight lines parallel to the wire
Loops from one end of the wire to the other
questions.explain: The field around a straight wire forms concentric circles centred on the wire.

questions.q: Which change would increase the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field?
options: Increasing the current in the wire
Reducing the strength of the magnetic field
questions.explain: Since F = BIL, increasing the current (or field, or length) increases the force.

questions.q: How can a voltage be induced in a coil of wire?
options: By moving a magnet into or out of the coil so the magnetic field through it changes
By keeping a magnet perfectly still inside the coil
By painting the coil with iron
questions.explain: Electromagnetic induction requires a changing magnetic field through the coil.

questions.q: A step-up transformer increases the voltage. How do its coils compare?
options: The secondary coil has more turns than the primary coil
The primary coil has more turns than the secondary coil
Both coils have exactly the same number of turns
The secondary coil has no turns at all
questions.explain: In a step-up transformer the output (secondary) coil has more turns, giving a higher output voltage.

questions.q: Why is electrical energy transmitted across the National Grid at very high voltage?
options: It lowers the current, which reduces energy lost as heat in the cables
It makes the current larger to deliver more power
It removes the need for transformers
It stops the cables from producing a magnetic field
questions.explain: High voltage means low current, and lower current greatly reduces heating losses in the transmission lines.

questions.q: A wire of length 0.2 m carries a current of 3 A at right angles to a magnetic field of flux density 0.5 T. What is the force on the wire?
A transformer has 1000 turns on the primary and 200 turns on the secondary. If the primary voltage is 230 V, what is the secondary voltage?
A 100% efficient transformer has a primary supply of 230 V at 2 A and a secondary voltage of 46 V. What is the secondary current?
questions.explain: For an ideal transformer VpIp = VsIs, so Is = (230 × 2)/46 = 10 A.

questions.q: Using Fleming's left-hand rule, which finger represents the direction of the current?
questions.explain: Thumb = motion (force), First finger = Field, seCond finger = Current.
